questions.q: Why was Jemima annoyed at the start of the story?
choices: She was not allowed to hatch her own eggs
Her sister-in-law took her best shawl
The farmer's wife would not let her fly
The collie-dog Kep ate up all her corn
questions.evidence: who was annoyed because the farmer's wife would not let her hatch her own eggs

questions.q: What was Jemima wearing when she set off?
choices: A coat and a pair of goloshes
A shawl and a poke bonnet
A cap and a little apron
A red handkerchief and clogs
questions.evidence: She was wearing a shawl and a poke bonnet.

questions.q: What was the gentleman doing when Jemima first saw him?
choices: Counting some eggs
Reading a newspaper
Picking some fox-gloves
Chopping wood for a fire
questions.evidence: an elegantly dressed gentleman reading a newspaper

questions.q: What kind of animal was the gentleman with sandy whiskers?
choices: A big rat
A sly fox
A hound pup
A brown hare
questions.evidence: The foxy gentleman admired them immensely.

questions.q: What was the gentleman's shed full of?
choices: Bags of oats
Lots of feathers
Old soap-boxes
Onions and herbs
questions.evidence: The shed was almost quite full of feathers

questions.q: How many eggs did Jemima lay in the nest in the shed?
choices: Four eggs
Six eggs
Nine eggs
Twelve eggs
questions.evidence: she laid nine eggs in the nest

questions.q: Why did the gentleman ask Jemima to bring sage and onions?
choices: He wanted to plant a little herb garden
They were for stuffing a roast duck to eat
He needed them to keep the eggs warm
He liked to give them to his friends
questions.evidence: all the different sorts of herbs that are used for stuffing roast duck

questions.q: After Jemima told Kep the whole story, what did Kep do?
choices: Went to find two fox-hound puppies
Told the farmer's wife about the eggs
Followed Jemima up the cart-road at once
Went back to sleep by the kitchen door
questions.evidence: He went to look for two fox-hound puppies

questions.q: What happened to Jemima's eggs in the shed?
choices: They all hatched into ducklings
The gentleman took them to his winter house
The puppies gobbled them up
Kep carried them home to the farm
questions.evidence: the puppies rushed in and gobbled up all the eggs

questions.q: What is the lesson of this story?
choices: Ducks should always learn to fly much better
Do not trust a stranger just because he is polite
Always bring a big bag of corn on a long trip
Farm dogs are never good friends for a duck
questions.evidence: Jemima Puddle-duck was a simpleton: not even the mention of sage and onions made her suspicious.
